topic.title: Logical Operators
topic.description: Using AND, OR, and NOT operators

sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Logical operators help you make decisions in code by combining or modifying conditions. Think of them as the 'and', 'or', and 'not' of programming!

• How to use AND (`&&`), OR (`||`), and NOT (`!`) operators
• Combining conditions to control program flow
• Avoiding common mistakes with logical operators

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine you're at a coffee shop deciding what to order:
- **AND (`&&`)**: You want coffee **AND** a croissant (both must be true)
- **OR (`||`)**: You want coffee **OR** tea (either is fine)
- **NOT (`!`)**: You want **NOT** decaf (invert the condition)

Logical operators work the same way in code! They let you combine boolean conditions (true/false values) to make smarter decisions.

• **AND (`&&`)**: Both conditions must be true
  Example: `if (age > 18 && hasTicket)` - must be adult AND have ticket

• **OR (`||`)**: Either condition can be true
  Example: `if (isRaining || isCold)` - bring jacket if either is true

• **NOT (`!`)**: Flips true to false (and vice versa)
  Example: `if (!isEmpty)` - do something if NOT empty

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: && (AND) returns true only if both operands are true
|| (OR) returns true if at least one operand is true
! (NOT) reverses the boolean value: !true is false
Short-circuit evaluation: && stops if the first operand is false; || stops if the first is true
De Morgan's laws: !(a && b) is equivalent to (!a || !b)

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Logical operators combine boolean conditions to make decisions. `&&` = AND, `||` = OR, `!` = NOT - remember these symbols. Practice combining conditions with parentheses for clarity. Ready to use these in if-statements and loops next.

questions.question: What is the result of: true && false?
questions.explanation: The logical AND operator (&&) returns true only if both operands are true. Since one operand is false, the result is false.

questions.question: What is the result of: true || false?
questions.explanation: The logical OR operator (||) returns true if at least one operand is true. Since the first operand is true, the result is true.
